content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn how to play piano, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Learn to identify middle C and basic keyboard geography (20 minutes)
Step 2. Practice playing simple C major triads (45 minutes)
Step 3. Drill the F major scale with the left hand (2 hours)
Step 4. Memorize the names of the white keys (30 minutes)
Step 5. Study the concept of whole steps and half steps (1 hour)
Step 6. Perform a simple rendition of "Mary Had a Little Lamb" (10 minutes)
Step 7. Practice basic finger independence exercises (3 days)
Step 8. Learn how to use the sustain pedal correctly (2 hours)
Step 9. Practice playing five-finger patterns (1 hour)
Step 10. Study basic rhythm and time signatures (4 hours)
Step 11. Practice sight-reading simple melodies in 4/4 time (5 days)
Step 12. Learn to play "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" with both hands (3 hours)
Step 13. Purchase a beginner piano method book (1 hour)
Step 14. Watch an introductory video on proper posture (15 minutes)
Step 15. Learn the difference between treble and bass clef (30 minutes)
Step 16. Research the history of the piano (2 hours)
Step 17. Practice reading notes on the grand staff (1 week)
Step 18. Learn about sharp and flat symbols (45 minutes)
Step 19. Memorize the order of sharps in a key signature (1 hour)
Step 20. Learn how to sit at the piano with the correct bench height (5 minutes)
Step 21. Find a reputable local piano teacher or online course (2 days)
Step 22. Practice basic hand shapes and "claw" position (1 hour)
Step 23. Learn the fingerings for the C major scale (90 minutes)
Step 24. Study the interval of a fourth and a fifth (1 hour)
Step 25. Learn to identify the black keys in groups of twos and threes (10 minutes)
Step 26. Practice playing legato and staccato notes (2 hours)
Step 27. Practice crossing the thumb under the middle finger (3 hours)
Step 28. Draw musical notes on staff paper (1 hour)
Step 29. Memorize the lines and spaces of the treble clef (2 hours)
Step 30. Learn how to trim fingernails to the proper playing length (5 minutes)
Step 31. Set up a dedicated practice space in the house (3 hours)
Step 32. Buy a metronome for rhythm practice (30 minutes)
Step 33. Learn the basic function of the soft pedal (1 hour)
Step 34. Unpack and assemble the piano or keyboard (2 hours)
Step 35. Listen to famous piano concertos for inspiration (4 hours)
Step 36. Read the owner's manual for the digital keyboard (1 hour)
Step 37. Learn about the circle of fifths (5 hours)
Step 38. Learn to play a basic chromatic scale (2 hours)
Step 39. Practice basic ear training by matching pitches (1 day)
Step 40. Wash hands to keep the piano keys clean (2 minutes)
